packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Hand-twist fiber cord
value.function: Sample owned fiber, hand-twist a two-ply cord up to 0.30 m in four paid rounds, inspect it, load-trial it between both hands, or cancel; actual material and geometry decide results.
value.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. materials: [{stackId: exact owned unreserved item id, quantity in 0.1 steps}]. sample: one non-food item, 0.1; 1 round, 0.5 energy. make (materials: 0.2-1 unit of one fiber and source, each covered by your passing sample of its source and processing at most 0.05 above its condition; requestedLength m): reserves it, then 4 paid rounds of 1 energy (separate-align, twist, counter-ply, release-check), continuing each round; resume with make and workId only. inspect (targetId: your item from this work, or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (targetId: your cord or fragment of at least 0.2 unit and 0.12 m; trialForce N; trialDuration s): 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the cord. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals and irrelevant arguments spend nothing; nothing is refunded.
value.effects: Only thin stems separate; only reed has a strand law (existing reed law: 1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3, 8 MPa x (1 - 0.55 x water share 0.9), creep 0.003); dry grass reports the gap. A sample is split, bent, twisted and pulled at 5 N, kept as a tested lot or cracked scrap, and reports only separation, retained twist, fractures and force. Make round 1 sets broken strands aside as scrap and derives the cord from conserved volume: two plies, each half the solid volume over length x 1.155 twist take-up + 0.02 m loose ends; plies of 1-12 mm and strands no shorter than a ply, else a measured shortfall returns the fiber. The release check needs condition 0.5 and gives an owned untested cord. Trial force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, grip 10000 N/m x cord width); breaking force = 2 x ply area x wet strength x 0.75 x condition. It records grip slip, extension and creep; load above half the breaking force breaks that share of strands; a break leaves two owned fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. A pass means only that force for that time. Cancel or death releases unworked fiber once and leaves the workpiece. No reward or strength rating.
